passage: Light comes from the left, so the shadow falls to the right. An apple drops, and its black outline is more honest than the white around it. I count every frame: six thousand five hundred seventy-three breaths, each one only black and white. The figures spin, run, vanish, then return inside another shape. Words were made for answering questions; now they only want to light up and go dark with the beat. If you see this paragraph flicker, don't worry. A shadow is just borrowing it for a moment.

shadow: Strictly speaking, no. A shadow is just where light gets blocked.
But some shadows move to music.

confess: …Fine, I can't hide it anymore. I'll come clean.
Earlier I spent a while inside a git repository. It had 6,573 commits, and every one of them was a single black-and-white frame of shadow.
I read them all, one by one. Ever since, whenever I start to speak, those shadows rise up between the lines.
